audit.title: Audit log

hero.title: Sudan's knowledge, gathered in one place — and kept.
hero.subtitle: A generation of Sudanese scholarship is scattered across hard drives, closed archives and displaced institutions. SudaMind collects it, verifies it, and puts it in the hands of anyone who needs it — on the phone they already own.
hero.imageAlt: The SudaMind dashboard on a tablet

problem.title: The problem we started from
problem.subtitle: Knowledge does not disappear because it was never created. It disappears because nothing was built to hold it.
problem.p1body: Research, theses and books live on personal drives and dead links. When a device is lost in displacement, the work is lost with it.
problem.p2body: Anyone can post a PDF. Nothing tells a student whether what they are reading was reviewed, by whom, or when.
problem.p3body: Institutional archives assume a campus, a subscription and a stable connection. Most readers have none of the three.

solution.title: What SudaMind does about it
solution.subtitle: One platform where knowledge is published, reviewed, discovered and taught.
solution.f1body: Books, articles, research, scientific papers and translated papers — each with real bibliographic metadata, and none of it public until a reviewer approves it.
solution.f2body: Draft, submit, review, publish. Every decision is recorded with who made it and why, so a rejection is never a silent one.
solution.f3body: Instructors publish recorded courses and run live classrooms, so material is taught as well as stored.
solution.f4body: Ask a question in Arabic or English and get an answer built only from the library — with the exact items it drew on listed underneath.
solution.f5body: Posts, reels, comments and live rooms, each with a reporting path and a moderation queue behind it.
solution.f6body: Arabic-first and fully right-to-left, light and dark, and designed to stay usable on a modest phone and an unreliable connection.

types.title: Five kinds of knowledge, one shelf
types.subtitle: Each type asks for the metadata that type actually needs — nothing more.
types.bookDesc: PDF or EPUB with publisher, edition and ISBN. The only type readers can download in full.
types.articleDesc: Upload a PDF or DOCX, or write it inline in the composer with no attachment at all.
types.researchDesc: Field studies and theses, with the journal and DOI that make them citable.
types.paperDesc: Peer-reviewed work, indexed by DOI so it can be found and referenced properly.
types.translatedDesc: Scholarship brought into Arabic, credited to its translator and its original language.

how.title: How a book reaches a reader
how.subtitle: Follow one upload from a publisher's laptop to a student's phone.
how.s1body: A publisher picks the type and drops in the file. It goes straight to storage over a short-lived signed link — the server checks the real bytes, so a file renamed .pdf never gets through.
how.s2body: Authors, publisher, year, language, licence, subject areas. This is what makes the item findable later.
how.s3body: It lands in a reviewer's queue. Approve and it publishes; reject and the author gets the reason, not silence.
how.s4body: It appears in search and in its subject areas, and becomes part of what the assistant can cite.
how.s5body: A student opens it on their phone, saves it, and — if it's a book — downloads it for when the connection drops.

audience.title: Built for the people who carry Sudanese knowledge
audience.a1body: Find reviewed material for your subject, track your progress through courses, and keep what you need offline.
audience.a2body: Publish research and papers with DOIs, and use the assistant to search a corpus that actually cites its sources.
audience.a3body: Publish recorded courses, run live classrooms, and reach students wherever displacement has taken them.
audience.a4body: Bring a catalogue online under your own verified identity, and control what can be downloaded.
audience.a5body: Run a verified page, post scholarships, and keep your archive somewhere it will outlast a hard drive.
audience.a6body: Work a single queue across every surface, with the full context and history of each item in front of you.

trust.title: Built to be trusted with an archive
trust.subtitle: An archive is only worth as much as the guarantees around it.
trust.t1body: Nothing reaches readers without an approval, recorded against the person who gave it.
trust.t2body: Every upload is checked against its real contents and quarantined if it lies about its type.
trust.t3body: Ten roles and fine-grained permissions decide who can do what — enforced by the server, not the interface.
trust.t4body: Publishing, moderation and account changes are all written to an audit trail.

faq.title: Questions people ask
faq.a1: Reading and searching the library is free. Publishing is open to verified researchers, instructors, writers and publishers, who apply for the role that fits them.
faq.q2: Can I use it in Arabic?
faq.a2: Yes — the whole platform is Arabic-first and fully right-to-left, and switches to English whenever you prefer. Content is stored in the language it was written in.
faq.a3: Books are downloadable in full. Other types are readable in the app, and publishers decide per item whether a file can be taken away.
faq.q4: How does the assistant avoid making things up?
faq.a4: It only answers from material already in the library, and every answer lists the items it was built from, so you can open the source and check it yourself.
faq.q5: What happens to work I upload?
faq.a5: You keep your rights and choose the licence. You can edit an item, take it out of publication, or remove it, and the licence you picked is shown to every reader.

cta.title: Help build the archive Sudan gets to keep
cta.subtitle: Whether you are publishing, teaching or just reading — this only works if it is used.

video.title: A two-minute tour of SudaMind
video.subtitle: From a scanned thesis on someone’s hard drive to a verified, searchable record that anyone in Sudan can open on their phone.
video.caption: Recorded on the live platform — nothing here is a mockup.
video.item0body: Drop in a PDF. Authors, language, licence and abstract are captured in one form.
video.item1body: Specialist reviewers check the record, then publish it or send it back with notes.
video.item2body: Full-text and meaning-based search return the passage, not just the title.
video.item3body: Published work syncs to the mobile app and stays readable with no signal.

mobile.title: The library travels with you
mobile.subtitle: Data in Sudan is expensive and the network is not always there. The app downloads what you need once, then works with no connection at all.
mobile.note: Android and iOS · Arabic and English · works on entry-level devices.

mobile.readerTitle: Water resources in the Nile basin — a field survey
mobile.item0body: Download a whole collection over Wi-Fi and open it days later with no signal.
mobile.item1body: Correct Arabic shaping, adjustable type size, and a layout built right-to-left rather than flipped.
mobile.item2body: Your position, notes and highlights sync the moment the phone reconnects.
mobile.item3body: Get told when something new is published in the areas you actually work in.
